problem_text:
A logistics company needs to schedule 6 delivery trucks to transport goods through 6 distribution centers.

Each truck must follow a specific route represented as pairs (Center, Handling time),
where each pair indicates the distribution center where the truck must stop and the time required to handle the goods at that center.
The order of pairs shows the required sequence in which the trucks must visit the centers.

Truck routes:
* T1 follows the route: (C5, 8) → (C2, 8) → (C4, 5) → (C1, 1) → (C3, 4) → (C6, 9)
* T2 follows the route: (C6, 2) → (C2, 5) → (C4, 3) → (C3, 10) → (C5, 7) → (C1, 4)
* T3 follows the route: (C3, 6) → (C6, 4) → (C4, 6) → (C1, 8) → (C5, 4) → (C2, 5)
* T4 follows the route: (C3, 3) → (C2, 6) → (C6, 1) → (C1, 8) → (C5, 1) → (C4, 1)
* T5 follows the route: (C2, 1) → (C1, 6) → (C5, 7) → (C4, 3) → (C6, 4) → (C3, 8)
* T6 follows the route: (C4, 7) → (C2, 7) → (C3, 1) → (C5, 7) → (C1, 5) → (C6, 9)

Each handling operation must be completed without interruption once it begins,
and each distribution center can only handle one truck at a time.
The objective is to determine the processing sequence of all trucks at the distribution centers
so that the total completion time for all deliveries is minimized.
